clue.text: Made music together?

definitions.meaning: to compose is to write music, so this is the past tense of writing a piece
someone together is calm and self-possessed

explanation.surface: A question about whether people played or sang as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'together' looks like the group doing the music, but it is a second definition: a together person is collected.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music, and a collected, unflustered person is described with the same word.

clue.text: African fell? Secure with rope

definitions.meaning: a North African of Berber and Arab descent
a fell is a stretch of upland or high moorland in northern England
to tie up a boat at a quay with ropes

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa took a tumble and was tied down with a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions. 'fell' looks like a verb (fell over), but it is the northern English noun for open hill country.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African, an open upland heath, and tying a vessel up at a berth all share one word.

clue.text: Mean little devil interrupts broadcaster

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: Sky is a British television broadcaster
an imp is a small mischievous demon

explanation.surface: A nasty small demon keeps breaking into a TV or radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' here means stingy or meagre, not unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimpy portion is a stingy, meagre one, which is one sense of mean.

clue.text: Mostly inadequate body image?

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter, keeping most but not all of it

parts.note: scant means barely sufficient

explanation.surface: Someone's view of their own body is, for the most part, not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body image' suggests self-esteem, but here it is a medical picture of the inside of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital scan produces a picture of the inside of a patient's body.

clue.text: One wedding finally accepted by pair recently living in sin?

indicators.note: to be accepted by is to be taken inside, so these letters go within the others

parts.note: of late means recently
one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: finally picks out the very last letter of the word wedding

explanation.surface: A single wedding gets approval from a couple who were until lately cohabiting unmarried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living in sin' looks like the couple's past, but it is the definition: a description of a dissolute life.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate person is recklessly dissolute, the sort of immoral life the old phrase about sin describes.

clue.text: Name cut from show programmed earlier

indicators.note: cut from means a piece is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: to present is to show

explanation.surface: A name was edited out of a TV show that had been scheduled in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programmed' suggests a TV schedule, but it means set up in advance, as a dial or device is.
explanation.definitionFit: A preset setting is one fixed ahead of time, before it is needed.

clue.text: Type of jumper favoured by some equestrian team members

definitions.text: Type of jumper favoured by some equestrian team members

parts.words: Type of jumper favoured by some equestrian team members
parts.note: a jumper is a British sweater, and the team members are players of a horseback sport whose name is also given to a high-collared sweater

explanation.surface: A fashion note on the sweaters that riders on a team like to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a showjumping horse, but in British English a jumper is a sweater; polo is played on horseback, and the high rolled-collar sweater shares its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater with a high turned-over collar is named after the horseback sport.

clue.text: Put right fitting inside to toughen transport

indicators.note: inside tells us these pieces are put within the other word

parts.note: enure, a variant of inure, means to harden or accustom
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: Fit the correct part inside a vehicle to make it more robust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like vehicles, but here it is the verb meaning to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with delight, to fill them with rapture.

clue.text: Remedy after a king's injected poison

indicators.note: injected means put inside, so these letters go into the remedy

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A treatment followed after the monarch was given a toxic injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link here: the remedy, after A and R have been injected, is the poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a South American plant extract used on arrow tips to paralyse prey.

clue.text: Sound of contentment, accepting life finally is not so bad

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so a letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a cat purrs when contented

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word life

explanation.surface: A satisfied murmur, taking in that life in the end is not that awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so bad' is the definition: less bad, so more pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something less corrupt or tainted than another is less bad, more unsullied.

clue.text: Political publication reduced to clear

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a manifesto is a party's published statement of policy

explanation.surface: A party document was cut down to make it plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' looks like a verb (clear away), but it is the adjective: obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manifest is plain and obvious, evident to everyone.

clue.text: Scientist seeing psychiatrist, so miserable

indicators.note: miserable means in a sorry state, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A researcher in therapy is feeling very unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserable' turns the letters of PSYCHIATRIST and SO into a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in the physics of stars and galaxies is a kind of scientist.

clue.text: Doesn't pen right off? But one may

indicators.note: off means going wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone doesn't write off for a reply, but someone else might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges DOESNTPEN plus R. 'But one may' is the definition: one who may pen a reply, as in a survey or a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A respondent is someone who replies, perhaps by writing back.

clue.text: Beyond words, exceptionally fine fiction

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a fable is a made-up story

explanation.surface: An outstanding story so good it cannot be described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' looks like praise for the fiction, but it rearranges FINE into INEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too great to be expressed in speech is inexpressible.

clue.text: Debate's inconclusive, in the event

indicators.note: inconclusive means without its conclusion, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to discuss is to debate; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A discussion fails to settle anything, as it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the event' looks like a phrase meaning 'as it happened', but the event is the definition: a field event in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the heavy disc is a track and field athletics event.

clue.text: Rule out movement lacking wind and notes

parts.note: B and E are both musical notes
calm weather has no wind

explanation.surface: Ban any motion in still air and in music.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: to stop movement, as a ship without wind is held still.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt a sailing ship by lack of wind is to stop it moving.

clue.text: For such a poet, doom isn't unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gloom is quite normal for a poet of this kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges DOOMISNT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of monodies, mournful odes for a single voice, is this kind of poet.

clue.text: Push drink before girl that's game in pub?

parts.note: to shove is to push
a half is a half-pint of beer
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Barge into a drink ahead of a girl, as one does in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOVE HALFPENNY is a British pub game sliding coins up a board; 'half' is a half-pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabletop pastime of sliding coins up a board, traditionally played in British taverns.

clue.text: Exercises, running up and down pitch?

definitions.text: Exercises, running up and down pitch?

parts.words: Exercises, running up and down pitch?
parts.note: musical practice drills that climb and descend through the notes, while the surface suggests training on a sports field

explanation.surface: Fitness drills, jogging back and forth along a football field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a sports field, but it is musical pitch: practice exercises going up and down the notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians practise sequences of notes ascending and descending in pitch.

clue.text: Mount a second colt before finish

parts.note: c is the abbreviation for colt in horse racing form guides
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Climb aboard a young horse just before the race ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' suggests getting on a horse, but it means to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a slope is to climb up it.

clue.text: Scoffing 50 per cent of tinned fish, mostly kept in reserve

indicators.note: fifty per cent of means half of the word is kept and half dropped

parts.note: sardines are commonly sold tinned

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is lost

parts.note: on ice means kept in reserve for later

explanation.surface: Gobbling half a tin of fish and keeping most of the rest back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffing' looks like eating, but it is mocking: half of SARDINES gives SARD, and ON ICE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mocking and derisive is like being scornful in tone.

clue.text: Expected behaviour for little boy

indicators.note: little points to the short pet form of the name, with its ending clipped off

parts.note: Norman is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A rule of conduct for a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' clips the boy's name NORMAN to its short form, losing AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard pattern of conduct is what is usual and accepted.

clue.text: Submitted front section to editor

parts.note: the bow is the front part of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone sent in the opening part of a piece to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submitted' suggests sending work in, but it means yielded.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in or yield to someone is to defer to them.

clue.text: Very small part one gets in week of festival

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, as in not a jot

definitions.text: one gets in week of festival
definitions.meaning: a word placed before week to name the festival week of Whitsun, Pentecost

explanation.surface: A tiny portion that someone receives in a holiday week.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes a word that goes in front of 'week' to name the week of the Pentecost festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount is a jot, and the word also names the Pentecost holiday, Whitsun.

clue.text: One inclined to be less yielding

definitions.meaning: someone or something that slopes or rests against another
less productive, as poor land gives less

explanation.surface: Someone tends to be stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tilts against something, and poorer harvests that produce less.

clue.text: Most wanting resolution to see it end

indicators.note: a resolution can be a working-out or rearrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The keenest determination to see it through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' looks like determination, but it rearranges SEEITEND.
explanation.definitionFit: The poorest people are those most lacking in necessities.
